slot.brief: Binomial distribution: given mean and variance (or two probability values), recover n and p, then compute a specific probability.

stem: A binomial random variable $X$ has mean $5$ and variance $\dfrac{5}{2}$. Find $P(X\leq 1)$.

verdicts.working: For a binomial variable, np=5 and np(1-p)=5/2, giving p=1/2 and n=10. Hence P(X≤1)=[C(10,0)+C(10,1)]/2^10=11/1024.

working:
$np=5$, $np(1-p)=\dfrac{5}{2}\Rightarrow p=\dfrac12$, $n=10$; $P(X\leq1)=P(X=0)+P(X=1)=\left(1+\binom{10}{1}\right)\left(\dfrac12\right)^{10}=\dfrac{11}{1024}$.

Independent check: For a binomial variable, np=5 and np(1-p)=5/2, giving p=1/2 and n=10. Hence P(X≤1)=[C(10,0)+C(10,1)]/2^10=11/1024.
solution:
For a binomial variable, $np=5$ and $np(1-p)=\dfrac{5}{2}$, so $p=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $n=10$.
$$P(X\leq 1)=\left[\binom{10}{0}+\binom{10}{1}\right]\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{10}=\dfrac{11}{1024}$$
